title: Validated Morse message codec
instructions:
Implement International Morse encoding for ASCII letters A–Z and digits 0–9.

## Files
- `morse.py`

The `CODES` dictionary in the starter supplies the exact alphabet and must remain
available. Implement these public helpers and class methods:
- `normalize_text(text: str) -> list[str]`: accept ASCII letters (either case),
  digits, and any character for which `str.isspace()` is true. Reject every other
  character with `ValueError`, including non-ASCII letters. Return uppercase
  words after splitting on arbitrary runs of whitespace. Empty/whitespace-only
  input returns `[]`.
- `split_morse(message: str) -> list[list[str]]`: parse the wire format described
  below into words containing code tokens. It validates formatting and that
  tokens contain only dots/dashes, but does NOT require tokens to exist in CODES.
  Invalid formatting raises `ValueError`; the empty string returns `[]`.
- `MorseCodec()` takes no arguments.
- `encode(text: str) -> str`: use `normalize_text`, replace each character with its
  code, join characters by one ASCII space, and join words by exactly `" / "`.
  Empty/whitespace-only plaintext encodes as `""`.
- `decode(message: str) -> str`: use `split_morse`, reject unknown code tokens with
  `ValueError`, and return uppercase plaintext with one ASCII space between words.
  The empty string decodes as `""`.

Wire format is canonical: nonempty words, nonempty tokens of dots/dashes,
exactly one ASCII space between tokens, and exactly `" / "` between words.
Reject leading/trailing spaces, repeated spaces, tabs/newlines, bare slashes,
empty words and other characters. Do not silently trim or repair wire messages.
All input arguments are strings. There are no punctuation codes.
